page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM hypervisor virtualization. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, the instance features 32 physical CPU cores and 64 vCPUs via Hyper-Threading. Hardware capabilities include 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache, along with extended instruction support including AVX-512 and AES cryptography. It features 128.0 GB of memory, providing a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio equivalent to 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance carries no local NVMe storage and includes no discrete GPU hardware, relying entirely on remote block storage while providing a 20 Gbps baseline network interface.

Performance profile highlights reveal a clear distinction between single-threaded and parallel compute workloads. Single-core throughput is constrained, registering bottom 25% scores in stress-ng single-core testing and Geekbench single-core performance (1017.0), alongside bottom 10% single-threaded gzip compression performance. Conversely, multi-threaded execution leverages the 64 vCPUs effectively, delivering top 25% performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (201.55 GB/sec) and average middle-tier performance across multi-core stress-ng, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and Redis SET operations (44.2 million ops/sec). Memory read and write bandwidth also hold steady in the middle 50% percentile across small and large block tests.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c5.16xlarge offers high core density suited for parallelized compute tasks without incurring the added cost of local storage or GPU hardware. The absence of local disk drives requires architectural reliance on network storage for persistence. Suitable workloads include multi-threaded batch processing, software compilation with compilers like Clang, parallel data transformation, static web serving, and general-purpose microservices requiring high multi-vCPU density.

Benchmark results indicate lower single-threaded throughput, with single-core Geekbench and stress-ng scores placing in the bottom 25%. However, its high vCPU count enables solid multi-core performance, highlighted by top 25% multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speeds and average middle-tier results in Redis operations, static web serving, and PassMark tests. The 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio makes this configuration cost-efficient for core-heavy parallel computing, batch execution, software compilation, and web serving workloads.
